title: Berlin Bulky Waste - Quick Summary
items: **Three cubic metres is the line everything turns on.** A recycling yard takes that much old furniture free per vehicle, and a full Multivan boot is roughly that. Above it the yard refuses the load rather than taking part of it.

**Partial unloading is not allowed.** Turn up with four cubic metres and you drive all four home again. BSR's own example: four cubic metres of furniture plus a fridge, the fridge is accepted and the furniture is sent away.
**Electrical appliances are always free and never counted.** Fridges, washing machines, televisions, cables, in household quantities, with no volume limit at any of the fourteen yards.

**A collection to your door is €50 or €100.** The saver fee is €50 for up to five cubic metres and comes from the sixteenth working day, the standard fee is €100 and comes inside fifteen. Electricals and clean bagged textiles ride along free.
**Rubble is the expensive one.** Tiles, brick and concrete cost €4 per started ten litres, which is €400 a cubic metre, and no collection will take it at any price.
**Paint, solvents and weedkiller are free up to 20 kg per type per day,** but only at the five yards with a hazardous waste counter.

**Leaving it on the pavement is the costly option.** Berlin's fine catalogue starts at €300 for one small item and runs to €11,000 above a cubic metre. Anything with hazardous parts, so a fridge or a television, reaches €15,000.
